Chapter 8: Living with Intention and Courage
There comes a moment when the question changes from, "What do I want?" to something deeper—like, "How do I want to live?"
Living with intention is all about making choices on purpose, instead of just drifting through life on autopilot. It's about deciding what truly matters to you, and having the courage to go after it, even when it feels tough.
Picture this: there's a woman who's spent years in a job that's comfortable, but not really fulfilling. She starts to feel this restless energy building up inside her. She dreams about starting her own business, but, let's be real—fear keeps holding her back. Fear of failing, fear of what others might think, and fear of stepping into the unknown.
Then, one evening, after a long walk, something clicks for her. She realizes that staying stuck is actually costing her more than the risk of just trying. That moment of clarity? It changes everything.
So, she starts small. She carves out a little time each week to work on her idea. Reaches out to people who've taken similar leaps, listens to their stories, and learns from their ups and downs. With every tiny step, her confidence grows. Was the journey easy? Not at all. There were setbacks, doubts, and moments where she wondered if she'd made a mistake. But with each step, she felt more alive—and more like herself.
Here’s something a lot of people miss: Courage isn't about not being afraid. It's about choosing to act, even when you're scared. Living with intention means saying yes to what lights you up, and no to what doesn't fit your values—even if that means standing out or being misunderstood.
There's a quiet strength in setting boundaries—in choosing how you spend your time and energy. Maybe you put family ahead of working late, or choose creativity over just fitting in. Sometimes, people might question your choices. But over time, those decisions add up, and you start to build a life that feels real and meaningful.
It’s easy to fall into the trap of waiting for the “right” moment to make a change. But honestly? That perfect moment almost never comes. What really matters is being willing to start, to take small steps, and to keep learning as you go.
Remember this: The life you want is built one choice at a time. You don’t have to have all the answers. What matters is asking the right questions—and having the courage to move forward, even when the path ahead isn’t completely clear.
